title: Stellar Protocol Canary report, schemaVersion 1
description: The `stellar-canary check --format json` report contract (CF-01). Required fields follow CF-01 section 3; everything else is optional, and an absent optional field means *not recorded*, never a default. Consumers must ignore properties they do not know: schemaVersion 1 only grows additively, and this schema therefore sets no `additionalProperties` restrictions.

schemaVersion.description: The report format version. This schema validates version 1 only; an unsupported version makes the whole report invalid.

toolVersion.description: The Canary CLI's own semver, independent of schemaVersion and targetProtocol. Informational; never use it for feature detection.

targetProtocol.description: The Stellar protocol version this run checked against.

name.description: Directory name of the project root. Arbitrary text; never render as markup.

type.description: The effective project type: detected or overridden by configuration.

network.description: Live network identity, present only when a live surface (rpc or soroban) was enabled. Its absence marks a fully offline run; it is not an error.

name.description: testnet, mainnet, futurenet, or a custom network name.

observedProtocol.description: What the endpoint reported via getNetwork. Compare it against targetProtocol rather than assuming the two match; absent when the live call failed.

error.description: Why the network identity could not be observed.

status.description: The single overall outcome. `error` means at least one result errored and outranks the pass/warning/fail policy decision — the same precedence as exit code 3.

counts.description: Convenience aggregates over results only. Skipped fixtures are counted separately and are never included in total. Always re-derivable from results[].status.

results.description: One entry per fixture that actually ran; never includes skipped fixtures. An empty array is a valid shape but is never compatibility evidence on its own (CF-01 section 7).

protocol.description: The fixture's own declared protocol; equals targetProtocol, since fixtures for other protocols are skipped before execution.

status.description: `skipped` is reserved: entries in results[] are check results that ran, never skips.

summary.description: One-line human-readable outcome. Arbitrary text; never render as markup.

details.description: Multi-line explanation, present when there is something further to say. Absent, not null, otherwise.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock time for this fixture. Not stable; ignore it in any comparison.

fixtureId.description: Currently always equal to testId; may be null when not recorded.

source.description: `live` (executed in this run) or `cache` (replayed from the local result cache, so a recording of an earlier run). Absent means *not recorded* — a report written before the field existed — and a value this version does not know is read the same way, never as live.

skipped.description: Fixtures the planner decided not to run, and why. Omitted entirely — not an empty array — when there are none; consumers must treat an absent list as empty.

reason.description: Free-form prose, e.g. "fixture targets protocol 27, this run targets protocol 28". Arbitrary text; never render as markup.

code.description: Stable machine-readable skip reason (UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL, SURFACE_DISABLED, MISSING_CAPABILITY, OFFLINE, NETWORK_MISMATCH or UNKNOWN). Absent in reports written before the field existed; consumers must ignore codes they do not know.

git.description: Build context of the checkout under test. Always present from 0.1.1 onward, with null fields when unavailable (not a Git repository, detached HEAD, no git executable); absent in older reports, which means *not recorded*. Never an error.

run.description: Build provenance of the engine. Absent means *not recorded* (a report written before the field existed); a recorded run whose commit is unknown carries an explicit null. Deliberately carries no timestamp, so two builds of one commit stay byte-for-byte comparable.

toolBuildCommit.description: The Git commit the binary was built from, or null when it was built without Git history.
